record.original_question: For a pair (C, G) satisfying condition (N), what groups can occur as the second lower ramification group G_2?

evidence.quote: We denote the ramification groups in lower numbering by G_i (i >= 0).
Question 6.5 What are the possible groups that can occur for G2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic p > 0, and let C be a smooth projective connected curve over k of genus g ≥ 2. Let G be a finite subgroup of the automorphism group Aut_k(C), and assume the pair (C, G) satisfies the following "condition (N)": there is a unique point P ∈ C(k) such that the stabilizer G_0(P) = {σ ∈ G : σ(P) = P, σ acts trivially on the residue field} equals G, the inertia group G acts with a single (wild) ramification point P on C, and |G|/g > 2p/(p−1) (so that (C,G) is a "big action" in the standard sense). For i ≥ 0, define the i-th lower ramification group at P by
   G_i = { σ ∈ G : v_P(σ(t) − t) ≥ i + 1 },
where t is a uniformizer of the local ring O_{C,P} and v_P denotes its normalized valuation. Determine all finite groups that can occur as the second lower ramification group G_2 for some pair (C, G) satisfying condition (N).
artifact.category_tag: automorphisms of curves in positive characteristic
artifact.status_search_result: No direct evidence was found indicating that the classification of possible second lower ramification groups G_2 under condition (N) has been completed. The question appears in a problem collection from a 2004 workshop on automorphisms of curves; subsequent work on "big actions" by Lehr–Matignon, Matignon–Rocher and others has produced partial results restricting the structure of G_2 (e.g., G_2 is often abelian of exponent p in known families), but a complete classification does not appear in the literature accessible via search.
